sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: A group of States sued the Government in the District of Massachusetts. The States contended that the Order unconstitutionally infringes on their authority to administer elections. This dispute centers on the States' claimed authority to manage their own election processes.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Opinion — file page 1, lines 1-31

sections.heading: Why this case reached the Court
paragraphs: The District Court agreed with the States and enjoined the Government from implementing the Order. The Government then asked the Supreme Court to stay that injunction. The Government argued it is likely to succeed on the merits of its jurisdictional argument.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Docket — file page 1, lines 1-80
Official Supreme Court Opinion — file page 1, lines 1-31

sections.heading: The legal issue
paragraphs: The legal issue was whether the States lacked a justiciable dispute because the Order did not injure them.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Opinion — file page 2, lines 1-38

sections.heading: What the Supreme Court did
paragraphs: The Government asked the Supreme Court to stay the injunction pending appeal. The Supreme Court agreed with the Government's request. The Supreme Court granted the stay, providing interim relief to the Government.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Opinion — file page 1, lines 1-31

sections.heading: Why the Court did it
paragraphs: The States lack standing to challenge §2(b) for much the same reason: It does nothing to them.
